passages.title: A Family Gathering
passages.text:
My grandmother Lan is a **widow**. She **got married** at nineteen, and for almost fifty years she lived in the same village as my grandfather, until his sudden death in 2015 – a **tragedy** that the whole family still finds hard to talk about. Today she lives with my uncle Minh, and although the two of them rarely agree about politics, they **get on well with** each other.

Last month the family gathered to celebrate my cousin Hoa's engagement. Hoa plans to **get married to** a young engineer she met at university, and everyone was delighted – except that her father had a long **dispute** with the groom's family over who would pay for the ceremony. Fortunately, my grandmother stepped in. "When I **married** your grandfather," she said, "we had almost nothing, yet we were happy." Her words calmed the argument, and both families agreed to share the cost. By the end of the evening, everybody was laughing as if nothing had happened.
passages.summary_vi: Cả nhà họp mặt mừng đám hỏi; bà nội, một góa phụ, hoá giải cuộc tranh cãi về chi phí đám cưới bằng câu chuyện của chính mình.

passages.title: Haggling at the Weekend Market
passages.text:
Every Saturday my aunt Thu takes me to the old market near our house. She enjoys the noise and the colour, but her real talent is bargaining. "You must always **haggle**," she tells me. "If you accept the first price, the seller will think you are a tourist." Last week she managed to **haggle over the price** of a silk scarf for almost ten minutes, and finally saved a third.

Thu is just as careful with her finances. As a student she borrowed some money from a friend, and she still remembers how uncomfortable it felt to **owe someone money**. "I worked two jobs just to **pay back money** I had borrowed, and I promised myself I would never do it again," she says. These days she checks her account every week to make sure she continues to **be in credit**.

At the food stalls she is equally strict. She never buys **raw meat** that has been left in the sun, and she prefers soup made with **barley**, a cereal that is cheap, filling and good for the heart. Her advice? Stay calm, smile, and walk away if the price is still too high.

passages.title: Learning First Aid
passages.text:
Last weekend I joined a first aid course at my local community centre. The instructor, a nurse called Ms Carter, began with the most common accident in any kitchen. "If you **cut yourself**, don't panic," she said. "Most small cuts **bleed** a lot at first, but the bleeding usually stops if you press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth." She then showed us how to **put a bandage around** an injured finger without making it too tight.

The second half of the course was about minor illnesses. A parent may sometimes need to **give someone some medicine** – a child with a headache, for example – but only after reading the label carefully. Adults who **feel sick** after a heavy meal can usually **take some tablets** and rest, whereas anyone with a high temperature that lasts more than two days should **see a doctor**. "If you are not sure which medicine is suitable, **go to the chemist** and ask the pharmacist for advice," Ms Carter added. I left the course feeling much more confident.
passages.summary_vi: Một buổi học sơ cứu: cách xử lý vết cắt, băng bó, dùng thuốc và khi nào nên đi khám.

passages.title: Living with Illness
passages.text:
My grandfather Quang smoked for forty years, so it was no surprise when doctors found that he had **lung cancer**. At first he ignored the signs: a dry cough and a dull **ache** in his chest that never seemed to go away. "It doesn't **hurt** very much," he kept saying. By the time he finally agreed to **go into hospital**, the illness was already serious, and the treatment that followed was long and **painful**.

Doctors warn that anyone who smokes heavily could **be likely to** develop serious lung problems, and many smokers also **suffer from** high blood pressure. Another danger is a **heart attack**, which can happen suddenly, even to people who seem healthy. "It is **likely** that your grandfather's lifestyle contributed to both problems," one doctor told us.

Fortunately, my grandfather recovered and has not touched a cigarette since. He now spends his mornings in the garden and tells his grandchildren, "Don't wait for the pain to start before you take care of your body."
passages.summary_vi: Ông Quang hút thuốc 40 năm, mắc ung thư phổi vì chủ quan; sau khi hồi phục ông khuyên các cháu chăm sóc cơ thể sớm.

passages.title: A Long Drive to the Mountains
passages.text:
Dung, an English teacher, was driving to a language conference in the mountains when he saw a sign beside the narrow road: **no overtaking**. He sighed, because the lorry in front of him was crawling uphill and there was no way to pass it. Then his phone's map stopped working, and he took a wrong turn. "If I'm not careful, I'll **end up** in the middle of nowhere," he muttered.

An hour later he reached a small village where a wedding party was taking place. Music was playing, and as the evening went on the guests began to **get wild**, dancing in the street and singing at the top of their voices. A local man invited Dung to join them. They talked about their jobs, and Dung discovered an unexpected **work-related connection**: the man's sister was a teacher at the very conference he was heading for.

Before leaving, Dung wanted to check an English word on a menu, so he stopped to **look something up** in the dictionary he always kept in the car. The word began with a double **consonant**, a sound that his students often find difficult to pronounce. The next morning he arrived at the conference only slightly late, and with a great story to tell.
passages.summary_vi: Chuyến lái xe lạc đường của thầy Dũng dẫn tới một đám cưới làng và một mối liên hệ bất ngờ về công việc.

passages.title: Exam Season in London
passages.text:
For most students, the end of the semester means one thing: exams. My sister Linh, a second-year student in London, has to **pass an exam** in economics before she can move on to the next stage of her degree. She began to **revise for** it a month ago, making colourful notes and testing herself with past papers every evening.

"I don't need to be perfect," she told me on the phone, "but I want to **do well**." Her tutor gave her simple advice: **do your best** and don't compare yourself with other people. Her own motto is even shorter: **try your best**, then accept the result. In Britain, students usually talk about wanting to **get a good mark**, while in the United States they speak of trying to **get a good grade**, but the meaning is the same: a high score that shows you understood the course.

Linh also knows that stress can harm performance, so she goes for a walk every afternoon and sleeps at least seven hours a night.

passages.title: A Week of Coursework
passages.text:
Minh, a final-year student, has a busy week ahead. He has to **do an essay** on climate policy and also **do exam preparation** for three subjects. He wonders whether he can **get through something** as big as a four-hundred-page textbook in only seven days.

His teacher, however, reminds the class that good **revision** is not about reading everything again and again. Instead, she says, students should **work on something** specific every day, such as a weak topic or a difficult type of question. "Short, regular sessions are better than one long night," she adds.

Minh has decided to **do some revision** each morning before lectures and to leave the evenings for writing. He knows that his final **grade** depends on both the essay and the exam, so he cannot ignore either. Last term the **mark** he received for one assignment was lower than he expected because he had not read the question carefully. This time he is keeping a diary of his **exam preparation**, so that he can see his progress at a glance.

items.definition: The activity of studying again what you have already learned.
items.explain: Revision (danh từ) = việc ôn tập.

items.definition: To spend time and effort improving or completing something.
items.explain: Work on sth = tập trung cải thiện/làm một việc cụ thể.

items.definition: To study again what you have learned before a test.
items.explain: Do some revision = ôn bài một chút.

items.definition: A score or level given for a student's work (especially American English).
items.explain: Grade = điểm số/xếp loại (chủ yếu Anh-Mỹ).

items.definition: A score given for a student's work or test (especially British English).
items.explain: Mark = điểm số (chủ yếu Anh-Anh).

items.definition: The process of getting ready for an exam.

exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence with a word or phrase from the box. Use the exact form given.

items.q: Our teacher asked us to ____ about the effects of social media.
items.explain: Giao bài viết luận: do an essay.

items.explain: Get through + khối lượng việc lớn.

items.q: If you want to improve your speaking, pick one weak area and ____ it every day.

items.explain: Điểm A là grade (chấp nhận cả mark).

items.q: He was disappointed with his ____ because he lost points for spelling.
items.explain: Mất điểm chính tả nên điểm số thấp: mark.

items.q: A little ____ every evening is better than studying all night.
items.explain: Danh từ không đếm được sau "a little": revision.

items.q: Students who ____ regularly feel less nervous on the day of the test.
items.explain: Sau who + V: do exam preparation.

items.q: I'll ____ tomorrow morning so I don't forget the grammar rules.
items.explain: Will + V: do some revision.

items.q: Good ____ includes practising past papers and timing yourself.
items.explain: Danh từ làm chủ ngữ: exam preparation.
